filename: A U.S. Scientific Community Vision for Sustained Earth Observations of Greenhouse Gases to Support Local to Global Action.pdf
title: A U.S. Scientific Community Vision for Sustained Earth Observations of Greenhouse Gases to Support Local to Global Action
processes: atmospheric boundary layer mixing and transport
testbed_rationale: This is a commentary and vision paper presenting Earth observation system strategies for greenhouse gases; no datasets were produced, analyzed, or released.
pain_points: Observational and scale gap at 10–100 km and decadal time scales for resolving diffuse carbon fluxes and biomass changes
Column-integrated satellite GHG observations integrate long-range horizontal and vertical transport, masking local surface boundary-layer signals
Persistent cloud cover limiting optical/lidar remote sensing in the humid tropics
SAR biomass saturation in dense, high-biomass forests
Over-reliance on short-lived inquiry-driven research missions rather than sustained, low-latency operational observing systems
extraction_notes: Commentary article based on a September 2024 scientific workshop. Machine learning is briefly mentioned as a tool for upscaling surface observations via remote sensing data fusion (citing McNicol et al., 2023; Reichstein et al., 2022), but no ML methods are implemented or evaluated here. Data Availability Statement confirms no data were used or created.
